text:
Priya: Ugh ISP out at my place. Fired up the backup satellite hotspot and my dog fell asleep on it. Pics later. Anyone have tips for stabilizing Starlink-ish portable units during storms? :satellite: :dog:
Jon: pls pic or it didn’t happen :laughing: last time my dog sat on the router it started barking at 2am
Priya: uploading a terrible phone pic now — Mochi the dog is *very* committed. Throughput is ~8 Mbps down / 2 Mbps up. Usable for Slack but not for video.
Luca: If it’s a little dish, try elevating to window height and clear line of sight. Also putting it on a small cardboard box helped me once.
Maya: Tethering to phone can be surprisingly better for latency if your carrier isn’t congested (and no dog sits on your phone).
Priya: Phone hotspot was worse here (carrier congested). This is a portable Ku-band unit I borrowed — quick setup I used: ```power on -> wait 60s -> check LED: solid blue = online```
OpsBot: Incident auto-log: ISP outage reported in Oregon region (1 user affected) — ticket #34321
Sam: Pro tip: put the unit on a windowsill and rotate 20–30 degrees if signal seems flaky. I once squeezed +3 Mbps that way during a storm.
Jon: random poll: should RedInk (company lingo for emergency kit) include a tiny tripod and cable ties for WFH emergencies? :raised_hands:
Maya: +1 for tripod. Also a foldable window mount.
Luca: +1 cable ties and velcro straps. cheap and fixes 80% of dog-sit issues.
Priya: Thanks everyone — moving Mochi off the ottoman and trying the window. Will update with a less blurry pic. :heart:
